podcast of exploiting women’s vulnerabilities. “I would honestly compare Alex Cooper to an ambulance chaser,” said @thebravomom. “Like, you just had the most horrific accident of your life, you’re hanging on by a thread, don’t know if you’re gonna make it, and she’s the first one there.”
“She wants to get the exclusive interview; she wants to be there when you’re vulnerable and you’re broken down, and you’re ready to sign over your rights to your life. Like, she’s so awful. And I wish that more women — celebrities, female athletes, reality stars — anyone who’s a woman on planet Earth, I wish they would stop making that their first stop after something happens in their lives, because she is profiting off of women’s heartaches and failures.”
“Alix Earle, hey girl, the passive-aggressive reposts and the likes and commenting on things — I got to call you out here,” Cooper said. “You're gonna need to get specific and just say what you got to say about me. There’s no NDA, no one is stopping you. Stop hiding behind other people and just say it yourself. What's the beef?”
“‘Cause I’m really tired of waking up and seeing you using this fake drama to distract from other shit going online for you. Not interested,” she said. “I know what happened, and so do you. So talk. Unless the fake narrative that you’re creating happens to be way more interesting than the truth.”
“I have nothing to hide when it comes to you and me, so unless you actually have something to say, I’m out. This is over,” she added.
Cooper tagged Earle directly in the caption of her video, which has garnered over 12 million likes on TikTok in under 24 hours. Earle actually hopped into the comments section to respond to Cooper’s video. “Okay on it!!” she wrote while reposting the TikTok to her own page.
Well then! We’ll keep you posted if and when anything else unfolds. Let us know what you think in the comments.
